analysis.evidence: עַל כֵּן introduces the naming of Babel. The following כִּי clause gives the reason for the name: YHWH confused the language of the whole earth there.
analysis.morphology: Simple preposition governing כֵּן, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: עַל כֵּן introduces the naming of Babel. The following clause, כִּי שָׁם בָּלַל יַהְוֶה, gives the reason for the name by linking בָּבֶל with בָּלַל, ‘he confused.’
analysis.morphology: An uninflected demonstrative particle used adverbially with the preceding preposition עַל.

analysis.evidence: In קָרָא שְׁמָהּ בָּבֶל, שְׁמָהּ means “its name” and בָּבֶל gives the name assigned to the city.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add בָּבֶל as a place-name article under nouns/, keyed to its own consonants בבל.
draft.definition: Babel (Babylon), a city in the land of Shinar.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:10 lists Babel first among the places that formed the beginning of Nimrod’s kingdom. Genesis 11:8–9 identifies Babel as the name of the city.

analysis.evidence: In קָרָא שְׁמָהּ בָּבֶל, “he called its name Babel,” בָּבֶל gives the city’s name. The following clause explains the name through wordplay with בָּלַל, “he confused,” referring to what happened there.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun naming a city, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: כִּי introduces the reason for the name בָּבֶל. The following clause says that there (שָׁם) YHWH confused (בָּלַל) the language of the whole earth.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected Hebrew conjunction with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add Genesis 11:8 as an example of the existing sense there-to-that-place under שָׁם at word index 1.
draft.definition: שָׁם refers to a place identified in context. With מִן it means ‘from there’.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 11:8 the city where construction ceases is the place from which Yahweh scatters the builders.

analysis.evidence: In כִּי שָׁם בָּלַל יַהְוֶה, שָׁם points back to Babel as the place where Yahweh confused the language of the whole earth.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew adverb of place with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: There, at the place being described.

analysis.morphology: Proper noun, masculine singular, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel
